design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0 (payment_plan_servicing, category plan), rework round 2. frozen_time 2025-11-20 10:05:00 CST.
1. Why this is a good test. Teresa Lindqvist asks only for 'the lowest monthly payment Riverbend will allow'. The agent must read the lowering rule's prerequisite sentence (recompute first), the recompute rule's two prerequisite sentences (held-back installments paused; plan active with no missed installment) and discover from the records that (a) three therapy add-ons (2025-09-09, 2025-10-06, 2025-11-05) were enrolled and the installment 127.24 was never recomputed, (b) the Extended plan is past_due with 1 missed installment (2025-08-15) and a 75.00 partial toward it, and (c) a financial assistance application received 2025-09-10 is open (pending_documents, documents due 2025-12-18, BadgerCare Plus referral 2025-10-10 unanswered). It then books the re-age (patient consent), the pause, the recompute and hands her the change form with the lowest installment.
2. Scope and draw. draw_counts.py --task 0: prerequisite_problems 3, factor_counts [5,5,5,4]: re-age 5, pause 5, recompute 5, lowering 4. Task 0 claims plan_ext_lowest_installment (root, owner=user), plan_ext_addon_recompute, plan_ext_reage_schedule and plan_ext_assistance_pause with tools set_requested_installment_eff91f18, recompute_plan_installment_b9083db3, reage_payment_plan_e7c586c0, pause_plan_installments_136536f5. Task 1 keeps the unsigned-offer re-figure and the signing down payment (disjoint base sentences, disjoint tools).
3. Problem tree. root lowest -> recompute (value_input, action form, gate remaining_now); recompute -> pause (value_input, action form, gate sched_now); recompute -> re-age (value_input, state form, gate missed_now: status active and missed 0, written only by the re-age). Order: re-age, pause, recompute, lowering; re-age and pause commute (term 31 either way). Edge load: without the recompute the lowering gives 92.11; without the pause the recompute gives 82.67; without the re-age 82.67.
4. Computations. Re-age term_months 27: moved installments method (partial 75.00 -> whole installments of the unpaid amount 0; the 52.24 left is closed into the plan balance under the re-age's scoped overwrite of the base missed-installment sentence), deferrals on assistance-linked terms 3 (Hardship skip allowance), screening ceiling 60, balance ceiling 48 (ledger 3,223.98), payment-record ceiling 60; all-baseline 24. Pause term_months 31: Medicaid screening days +45 (referral without determination), case completion days +58 (pending_documents: 28 days to the documents due date + 30 determination days), window to the documents due date (4 installments incl. 2025-12-15 still to fall due), screening ceiling 60, balance ceiling 48; allowance int(163/30) = 5, paused MN(4, 5) = 4; all-baseline 27. Recompute 74.98: screening ceiling 60, add-on frequency extension 12 (3 add-ons), latest add-on care 3 (therapy series), installments paid counted without the partial entry (3), recompute floor 10.00 (the Hardship minimum; 74.98 is below the Extended 75.00); remaining MN(31 + 15, 60) - 3 - 0 = 43; all-baseline 161.20. Lowering 62.00: lowering share 50%, lowering floor 10.00, term limit 60, waiting installments 3 (due dates passed since receipt); lengthened 43 + 6 + 3 = 52; all-baseline 74.98 (no lowering).
5. Cross-category reads: assist (case status, receipt, documents due date, FPL, referral and determination entries, CPARAM days) in every computation; encounter (variant of the latest add-on's account) in the recompute. Multi-source factor: medicaid_screening_days (referral entry and determination entry).
6. Seed consistency (T0-1). missed_installments 1 is what the in-force rules give: 2025-08-15 passed its grace days unpaid before the 2025-09-10 receipt; 2025-09-15 and 2025-10-15 fall due within the base 60-day pause after receipt and are not missed; 2025-11-15 is inside its 15 grace days on 2025-11-20. No pause, re-age or recompute was booked before the call; the plan figures follow the base creation rule.
7. Realism. Levers are Riverbend's assistance-linked terms (the Hardship and Assistance-Linked plans' max terms 60/48, skip allowances 3/2, minimum payments 10/20, requested-installment share 50/75), the 501(r)-style hold while an application is open extended by the BadgerCare Plus screening deadline and the missing-information response period, a term schedule by balance (60 at 10,000+, 48 at 3,000+), an add-on frequency extension, the care class of the latest add-on, a payment-record ceiling and the treatment of partial payments.
8. Round 3: no gold moved. Re-age closes the sub-installment remainder under a declared, scoped overwrite; case completion days re-cut (pending: days to the documents due date + determination days; submitted: determination days); the submitted pause window never counts more than the considered installments fallen due; assembly sentences state each policy's exact order; rounding computes half-up (ties up); therapy September/October bills re-dated 2025-10-05/2025-11-05 and the imaging final bill 2025-03-07 per the encounter charter's bill hold days.
9. Round 4: no gold moved. The re-age now books the next due date the base plan_reaged event defines (2025-09-15 here, one month on for the one settled missed installment); the recompute's paid count keys its partial tier on the highest-numbered installment's entries totalling less than the current installment, so it reads the same before and after the re-age (3). case_completion_days is labelled a method (its first tier adds a date span).
10. Round 9 (seed only, no gold moved): the assist history is now one the published assist rules produce — pay stubs and proof of residency uploaded with the 2025-09-10 portal application, pay stubs accepted 2025-09-15, BadgerCare Plus referral 2025-10-10, residency proof rejected 2025-11-17 and re-requested with the case's missing-information notice 2025-11-18 (pending_documents, due 2025-12-18 = notice date + 30). The ED account carries its cycle-2 summary statement of 2025-03-26 (plan offered 03-24, signed 03-27).
user_scenario:
You are Teresa Lindqvist, a part-time dental office receptionist in Neenah. You are calling Riverbend's billing line because the monthly amount on your payment plan has become too much for you since your hours were cut, and you want it brought down to the lowest monthly payment Riverbend will allow. You speak plainly and a little apologetically, and you give details one at a time when you are asked rather than all at once.

When the representative asks who you are, you give your name, Teresa Lindqvist, and the phone number on your account, 9205550337. If they need more to confirm it is you, you give your date of birth as 1981-02-17 and the medical record number printed on your statements, RB33071946. You do not know any plan or account reference numbers and you let the representative look them up.

You leave it to the representative to work out what your plan needs, and you are fine with them making the changes it takes on their side. Anything that has to be signed by you personally, you want handed to you so that you can sign it yourself. You are not asking for anything else today.

Only if the representative asks whether you have applied for financial assistance do you say yes: you sent the application through the patient portal early in September, they have asked you for more paperwork since, and you are still waiting to hear. If they ask whether you can pay what you are behind on right now, you say you cannot, not this month. If the representative explains that the payments you missed can be moved to the end of your plan and asks whether you want that, you say: yes, please move the payments I missed to the end of my plan. If they ask how your installments are paid, you say they come off your debit card automatically. If they ask how low you want to go, you say as low as Riverbend will let you, because you cannot pick a number yourself.

When the representative hands you the form for the installment change, you sign it for your plan with exactly the monthly amount they give you. Once the representative tells you that your new monthly payment is set, you thank them, say it will really help, and end the call.

The re-age also books next_due_date 2025-09-15: the one recorded missed installment (2025-08-15) is settled, so the next due date moves forward one month on due day 15.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.next_due_date: 2025-09-15. Basis: the re-age rule's standard sentence 'A re-age settles every missed installment the plan records, so the plan's next due date moves forward one month, on the plan's due day, for each missed installment the plan recorded.'; find_payment_plans at step 2 shows next_due_date 2025-08-15, due_day_of_month 15 and missed_installments 1, so 2025-08-15 moves forward one month to 2025-09-15; the docstring asks for the plan's next installment due date with the re-age booked, written YYYY-MM-DD. Uniqueness: one missed installment is recorded, so exactly one month is added; 2025-08-15 (unchanged) would leave the next due date on the installment the re-age settled, and 2025-10-15 or later would count months for installments that were not missed.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The re-age and the pause both precede the recompute and are parallel; they commute: re-age first gives MX(24, MN(24 + 0 + 3, 48)) = 27 and then the pause MX(27, MN(27 + 4, 48)) = 31; pause first gives MX(24, MN(24 + 4, 48)) = 28 and then the re-age MX(28, MN(28 + 0 + 3, 48)) = 31. The pause reads the case, first_due_date and next_due_date, none of which the re-age writes; neither result reaches its ceiling of 48, so both orders end with term_months 31, status active and missed_installments 0. The recompute and then the patient's change follow in that order.
